>To David: Here's some exploratory ways of testing the formulas that are smartphone-friendly and maybe less friction than pulling out a slidedeck or problem sheet. The first is more standard multiple choice problems (with hints/explanations) and then the next is a memory match (flip cards, match them to formulas by memory). Last is math-symbol-wordle to help learn the exact placement/ordering of the terms and disambiguate the "I knew there was a R in there somewhere..." issues. This is just a minimal proof of concept; I've come up with a lot more problems than just these that test circle Area/Circumference but I wanted to see if this format is something you're interested in

## Practice Questions

Answer each question, then check the **Hint** and **Solution** tabs if you need help.
Use the buttons below the questions to move between them, then press **Submit** when you're done.

### Question [1]{.slide-num} of 4 {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Which of the following equations correctly model the relationship between a circle’s Area $A$ and
Radius $r$ ?
<br>
(more than one correct choice)

<!--
  MULTIPLE-ANSWER QUESTION
  - Use type="checkbox" so more than one choice can be picked.
  - List every correct letter in data-answer, separated by commas.
-->
<form class="quiz-question" data-question="Question 1" data-answer="b,d">
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q1" value="a"> A. $A = (\pi r)^2$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q1" value="b"> B. $\frac{A}{r}=\pi r$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q1" value="c"> C. $A=\pi^2 r$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q1" value="d"> D. $A = \pi r^2$</label>
</form>

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
Demo of math diagrams

```{.tikz}

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1]
  \def\R{1.6}

  % ---------------- (1) Radius ----------------
  \begin{scope}[shift={(0,0)}]
    \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
    \draw[seg] (0,0) -- node[right] {$r$} (0,\R);
    \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
    \node at (0,-\R-0.55) {\small (a) Radius};
  \end{scope}

  % ---------------- (2) Area: the r^2 square ----------------
  \begin{scope}[shift={(4.6,0)}]
    \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
    % hatched r-by-r square in the upper-left quadrant
    \fill[pattern=north east lines] (-\R,0) rectangle (0,\R);
    \draw[seg] (-\R,0) rectangle (0,\R);
    \node[right] at (0,\R/2) {$r$};
    \node[below] at (-\R/2,0) {$r$};
    \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
    % r^2 call-out
    \node (lbl) at (-\R-0.6,\R+0.75) {$r^2$};
    \draw[callout] (lbl.south east) to[bend left=25] (-\R+0.35,\R-0.35);
  \end{scope}

  % ---------------- (3) Diameter ----------------
  \begin{scope}[shift={(9.4,0)}]
    \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
    \draw[seg] (0,-\R) -- (0,\R);
    \node[right] at (0,\R/2)  {$r$};
    \node[right] at (0,-\R/2) {$r$};
    \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
    \draw[dim brace] (\R+0.15,\R) -- node[right=11pt] {$2r$} (\R+0.15,-\R);
    \node at (0,-\R-0.55) {\small (c) Diameter $=2r$};
  \end{scope}
\end{tikzpicture}
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
    % (left) one quarter of the circle: two radii and the chord between their ends
    \begin{scope}[shift={(0,0)}]
      \def\R{1.6}

      \colorlet{sqcol}{red!65!black}     % dark red: square sides
      \colorlet{circcol}{blue!65!black}  % dark blue: circle
      \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
      \draw[seg, dashed] (-\R,0) -- (0,0) -- node[below, font=\footnotesize]{$r$}(\R,0);
      \draw[seg, dashed] (0,-\R) -- (0,\R);
      \draw[seg]
        (\R,0)  -- node[below=0pt, font=\footnotesize] {$x$}
        (0,\R)  -- node[below=0pt, font=\footnotesize] {$x$}
        (-\R,0) -- node[above=0pt, font=\footnotesize] {$x$}
        (0,-\R) -- node[above=0pt, font=\footnotesize] {$x$}
        cycle;
      \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
      % C call-out pointing to the circle
      \node(Clbl) at (\R+0.8,\R+0.2) {$C$};
      \draw[callout] (Clbl) -- (45:\R+0.05);
      \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
      \node[align=left] at (0,-2.6)
      {$C > \:x+x+x+x$};
    \end{scope}
\end{tikzpicture}
```
:::

### Solution

**Answer: B & D.**
<br>
**B**: <br>
$$
\begin{aligned}
    \frac{A}{r}&=\pi r \\
    r*\frac{A}{r}&=\pi r * r \\
    A&=\pi r^2 \\
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
:::

::: {.carousel-item}
### Question [2]{.slide-num} of 4 {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

A circle has radius $r$ and diameter $d$. Which of the following equations correctly relate $r$ and $d$?
<br>
(more than one correct choice)

<form class="quiz-question" data-question="Question 2" data-answer="b,d">
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q2" value="a"> A. $d = \frac{r}{2}$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q2" value="b"> B. $r = \frac{d}{2}$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q2" value="c"> C. $r = 2d$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q2" value="d"> D. $d = 2r$</label>
</form>

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
The diameter goes all the way across the circle through the center, so it's made of two radii placed end to end.

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
  \def\R{1.6}
  \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
  \draw[seg] (-\R,0) -- node[above] {$r$} (0,0) -- node[above] {$r$} (\R,0);
  \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
  \fill (-\R,0) circle (1.3pt);
  \fill (\R,0) circle (1.3pt);
  \draw[dim brace] (\R,0) -- node[below=11pt] {$d$} (-\R,0);
  \node at (0,-\R-0.55) {$d = r + r$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
Which is bigger, $d$ or $r$? An equation that makes the bigger one come out smaller is written backwards.
Test each choice with a real number, like $r = 3$ (so $d = 6$).
:::

### Solution

**Answer: B & D.**
<br>
Two radii make one diameter:
$$
\begin{aligned}
    d &= r + r = 2r \\
    \frac{d}{2} &= r
\end{aligned}
$$

**Why the others are wrong:** A and C put the 2 on the wrong side.
With $r = 3$: choice A gives $d = 1.5$ and choice C gives $r = 12$ when $d = 6$. In both cases the diameter comes out *shorter* than the radius, which can't happen.

:::
:::

::: {.carousel-item}
### Question [3]{.slide-num} of 4 {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Which of the following equations correctly give the circumference $C$ of a circle with radius $r$ and diameter $d$?
<br>
(more than one correct choice)

<form class="quiz-question" data-question="Question 3" data-answer="a,c">
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q3" value="a"> A. $C = 2\pi r$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q3" value="b"> B. $C = \pi r^2$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q3" value="c"> C. $C = \pi d$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q3" value="d"> D. $C = 2\pi d$</label>
</form>

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
Circumference is a *length*: the distance around the circle. If you cut the circle and unroll it, its edge is a little more than 3 diameters long. That "little more than 3" is $\pi \approx 3.14$.

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
  \def\R{0.8}
  \def\D{1.6}
  % the circle, sitting off to the left
  \draw[circ] (-1.6,\R) circle (\R);
  \draw[seg] (-1.6-\R,\R) -- node[above, font=\footnotesize] {$d$} (-1.6+\R,\R);
  \node[center dot] at (-1.6,\R) {};
  % the unrolled circumference
  \draw[red!65!black, line width=1.6pt] (0,0) -- ({pi*\D},0);
  \foreach \k in {0,1,2,3}
    \draw[seg] ({\k*\D},-0.12) -- ({\k*\D},0.12);
  \draw[seg] ({pi*\D},-0.12) -- ({pi*\D},0.12);
  \foreach \k in {1,2,3}
    \node[above, font=\footnotesize] at ({(\k-0.5)*\D},0.1) {$d$};
  \draw[dim brace] ({pi*\D},0) -- node[below=11pt] {$C = \pi d \approx 3.14\,d$} (0,0);
\end{tikzpicture}
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
Since $d = 2r$, try replacing $d$ with $2r$ in one choice and see whether it turns into another choice.
<br>
Also, a formula with $r^2$ gives *square* units (like ft²), which measures area, not length.
:::

### Solution

**Answer: A & C.**
<br>
**C** is the definition of $\pi$: the circumference is $\pi$ diameters long. Substituting $d = 2r$ gives **A**:
$$
\begin{aligned}
    C &= \pi d \\
      &= \pi (2r) \\
      &= 2\pi r
\end{aligned}
$$

**Why the others are wrong:**

- **B** ($\pi r^2$) is the *area* formula. It's the most common mix-up on the ACT.
- **D** ($2\pi d$) uses the "2" twice. Since $d$ already equals $2r$, $2\pi d = 4\pi r$, which is double the real circumference.

:::
:::

::: {.carousel-item}
### Question [4]{.slide-num} of 4 {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Which of the following equations correctly give the area $A$ of a circle in terms of its **diameter** $d$?
<br>
(more than one correct choice)

<form class="quiz-question" data-question="Question 4" data-answer="b,d">
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q4" value="a"> A. $A = \pi d^2$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q4" value="b"> B. $A = \pi \left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q4" value="c"> C. $A = \frac{\pi d^2}{2}$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q4" value="d"> D. $A = \frac{\pi d^2}{4}$</label>
</form>

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
The area formula you know uses the radius: $A = \pi r^2$. What do you replace $r$ with if you only know $d$?
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
A $d \times d$ square around the circle splits into four $r \times r$ squares.

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
  \def\R{1.6}
  \fill[pattern=north east lines] (-\R,0) rectangle (0,\R);
  \draw[seg] (-\R,-\R) rectangle (\R,\R);
  \draw[seg, dashed] (-\R,0) -- (\R,0);
  \draw[seg, dashed] (0,-\R) -- (0,\R);
  \draw[circ, blue!65!black] (0,0) circle (\R);
  \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
  \node[fill=white, inner sep=1.5pt] at (-\R/2,\R/2) {$r^2$};
  \draw[dim brace] (-\R,\R) -- node[above=11pt] {$d$} (\R,\R);
  \draw[dim brace] (\R,\R) -- node[right=11pt] {$d$} (\R,-\R);
  \node at (0,-\R-0.75) {$d^2 = 4r^2 \;\Longrightarrow\; r^2 = \frac{d^2}{4}$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
When you square a fraction, square the top **and** the bottom: $\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{d^2}{2^2}$.
:::

### Solution

**Answer: B & D.**
<br>
Replace $r$ with $\frac{d}{2}$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
    A &= \pi r^2 \\
      &= \pi \left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 \\
      &= \pi \cdot \frac{d^2}{4} = \frac{\pi d^2}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Why the others are wrong:**

- **A** uses the diameter as if it were the radius. That's 4 times too big.
- **C** squares the $d$ but forgets to square the 2. That's 2 times too big.

:::
:::

:::
:::

```{=html}
<button id="submit-quiz" class="btn btn-primary">Submit</button>
<div id="quiz-results" style="margin-top: 1em;"></div>

<script>
  // Turn "b, d" into ["b", "d"] (lowercase, trimmed, sorted)
  function parseAnswers(str) {
    return (str || "")
      .split(",")
      .map(s => s.trim().toLowerCase())
      .filter(s => s.length > 0)
      .sort();
  }

  // Format ["b", "d"] as "B, D" for display
  function formatLetters(letters) {
    return letters.length ? letters.map(l => l.toUpperCase()).join(", ") : "no answer";
  }

  // Score the quiz on submit.
  // Works for both radio (single-answer) and checkbox (multiple-answer) questions:
  // a question is correct only if the student picked EXACTLY the set of correct
  // answers, with nothing missing and nothing extra.
  document.getElementById("submit-quiz").addEventListener("click", () => {
    const questions = document.querySelectorAll(".quiz-question");
    let score = 0;
    let details = "";

    questions.forEach(form => {
      const name = form.dataset.question;
      const answers = parseAnswers(form.dataset.answer);
      const picked = Array.from(form.querySelectorAll("input:checked"))
        .map(input => input.value.trim().toLowerCase())
        .sort();

      const correct =
        picked.length === answers.length &&
        picked.every((letter, i) => letter === answers[i]);

      if (correct) score++;

      details += `<li>${name}: ${formatLetters(picked)} ${correct ? "✅" : "❌"}` +
                 (correct ? "" : ` <em>(correct: ${formatLetters(answers)})</em>`) +
                 `</li>`;
    });

    document.getElementById("quiz-results").innerHTML =
      `<h3>Score: ${score} / ${questions.length}</h3><ul>${details}</ul>`;
  });
</script>
```

### Memory Match [1]{.slide-num} of 2: Circle Formulas {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Flip two cards at a time. Match each formula **name** to its **formula**.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
memory([
  ["Area of a circle",     "A = \\pi r^2"],
  ["Circumference",        "C = 2\\pi r"],
  ["Diameter",             "d = 2r"],
  ["Equation of a circle", "(x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2"]
])
```

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
Area is measured in square units, so its formula squares the radius: $r^2$. Circumference is a length, so its radius isn't squared.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
The diameter is two radii long, so the formula for $d$ has a **2** in it. The equation of a circle is the only one with both $x$ and $y$.
:::

### Solution

| Name | Formula |
|:-----|:--------|
| Area of a circle | $A = \pi r^2$ |
| Circumference | $C = 2\pi r$ |
| Diameter | $d = 2r$ |
| Equation of a circle | $(x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2$ |

:::
:::

## How to play Wordle

- <span class="badge bg-success">Green</span>: right symbol, right spot. It stays filled in on your next try.
- <span class="badge wordle-yellow">Yellow</span>: the symbol is in the formula, but in a different spot.
- <span class="badge bg-secondary">Gray</span>: the symbol isn't in the formula.

### Wordle [1]{.slide-num} of 3: Area {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Finish the formula for the **area** of a circle.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
wordle("A =", ["π", "r", "²"])
```

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
Area is measured in **square** units (like ft²), so something in the formula gets squared.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
The formula uses the radius, not the diameter, and the constant $\pi$.
Careful: a plain **2** is a different symbol from the exponent **²**.
:::

### Solution

**Answer:** $A = \pi r^2$

The area is $\pi$ times the radius **squared**. The other keys are traps:

- **2**: belongs in the circumference formula, $C = 2\pi r$, not in the area formula.
- **d**: using the diameter instead of the radius gives an area 4 times too big.

:::
:::

::: {.carousel-item}
### Wordle [2]{.slide-num} of 3: Circumference {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Finish the formula for the **circumference** of a circle, using its **diameter**.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
wordle("C =", ["π", "d"])
```

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
Circumference is a **length**, not an area, so nothing gets squared.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
$\pi$ is defined as the number of diameters that fit around a circle: the circumference is a little more than 3 diameters long.
:::

### Solution

**Answer:** $C = \pi d$

This is the definition of $\pi$: $\pi = \frac{C}{d}$, so $C = \pi d$.

You may also know $C = 2\pi r$. It's the same formula written with the radius, since $d = 2r$, but this puzzle uses the diameter.

:::
:::

::: {.carousel-item}
### Wordle [3]{.slide-num} of 3: Diameter {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Finish the formula for the **diameter** of a circle, using its **radius**.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
wordle("d =", ["2", "r"])
```

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
The diameter goes all the way across the circle, through the center.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
How many radii, placed end to end, make one diameter?
:::

### Solution

**Answer:** $d = 2r$

The diameter is made of two radii placed end to end: $d = r + r = 2r$.

A common mistake is $d = \frac{1}{2}r$. That would make the diameter *shorter* than the radius, which can't happen.

:::
:::

:::
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What the symbols mean

| Symbol | Meaning |
|:------:|:--------|
| $A$ | **Area**: the space inside the circle (square units) |
| $C$ | **Circumference**: the distance around the circle |
| $d$ | **Diameter**: the distance across the circle, through the center |
| $r$ | **Radius**: the distance from the center to the edge |
| $\pi$ | **Pi**: about 3.14, the number of diameters that fit around a circle |
| $\theta$ | **Central angle**, in degrees |
| $^2$ | **Squared**: multiply a number by itself |
| $\frac{1}{2}$ | **One half** |
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
function memory(pairs) {
  const status = html`<p></p>`;
  const grid = html`<div style="display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr); gap:.5em; max-width:44em"></div>`;
  const resetBtn = html`<button class="btn btn-secondary mb-2">Reset & shuffle</button>`;
  let open, found, timer;

  function deal() {                          // build a fresh board
    clearTimeout(timer);                     // cancel a pending flip-back
    open = []; found = 0;
    status.textContent = `Pairs found: 0 / ${pairs.length}`;
    grid.replaceChildren();                  // remove the old cards
    const cards = d3.shuffle(pairs.flatMap(([name, f], id) =>
      [{id, face: () => html`<b>${name}</b>`}, {id, face: () => tex`${f}`}]));

    for (const card of cards) {
      const btn = html`<button class="btn btn-outline-primary" style="min-height:5em">?</button>`;
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if (open.length === 2 || open.some(o => o.btn === btn)) return;   // ignore 3rd click / same card
        btn.replaceChildren(card.face());
        open.push({...card, btn});
        if (open.length < 2) return;
        const [a, b] = open;
        if (a.id === b.id) {                                               // match: lock both cards
          for (const o of open) { o.btn.disabled = true; o.btn.className = "btn btn-success"; }
          open = [];
          status.textContent = ++found === pairs.length ? "All matched! 🎉" : `Pairs found: ${found} / ${pairs.length}`;
        } else {                                                           // no match: flip back
          timer = setTimeout(() => { for (const o of open) o.btn.textContent = "?"; open = []; }, 1200);
        }
      };
      grid.append(btn);
    }
  }

  resetBtn.onclick = deal;
  deal();
  return html`<div>${resetBtn}${status}${grid}</div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
function wordle(lhs, answer, keys = ["π", "r", "d", "2", "²", "C", "θ", "½"], maxTries = 6) {
  const look = {                       // [tile classes, key classes] for each result
    success:   ["bg-success text-white",   "btn-success"],
    warning:   ["wordle-yellow",           "wordle-yellow"],
    secondary: ["bg-secondary text-white", "btn-secondary"]
  };
  const tileCls = "border rounded fs-4 d-inline-flex align-items-center justify-content-center";
  const board = html`<div class="d-flex flex-column gap-1 mb-2"></div>`;
  const msg = html`<p style="min-height:1.5em"></p>`;
  const kb = html`<div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-1 mb-3"></div>`;
  const resetBtn = html`<button class="btn btn-secondary">Reset</button>`;
  const keyBtns = {};
  let typed, locked, row, tries, done;

  // Full guess: locked greens stay put; typed symbols fill the other blanks in order
  const full = () => { let j = 0; return answer.map((a, i) => locked[i] ? a : typed[j++]); };
  const blanks = () => locked.filter(x => !x).length;

  // Wordle rules: greens first, then yellows use up whatever answer symbols are left
  function score(g) {
    const left = answer.filter((a, i) => g[i] !== a);
    return g.map((s, i) =>
      s === answer[i] ? "success"
      : left.includes(s) ? (left.splice(left.indexOf(s), 1), "warning")
      : "secondary");
  }

  function newRow() {
    row = html`<div class="d-flex gap-1 align-items-center"><span class="fs-4 me-2">${lhs}</span></div>`;
    answer.forEach((a, i) => row.append(html`<span class="${tileCls} ${locked[i] ? look.success[0] : ""}"
      style="width:2.2em; height:2.2em">${locked[i] ? a : ""}</span>`));
    board.append(row);
  }

  function press(k) {
    if (done) return;
    if (k === "⌫") typed.pop();
    else if (k !== "Enter") { if (typed.length < blanks()) typed.push(k); }
    else if (typed.length < blanks()) { msg.textContent = "Fill every blank first."; return; }
    else {
      const g = full();
      score(g).forEach((c, i) => {
        row.children[i + 1].className = `${tileCls} ${look[c][0]}`;
        if (c === "success") locked[i] = true;                      // greens carry over to the next row
        const b = keyBtns[g[i]], rank = ["secondary", "warning", "success"].indexOf(c);
        if (rank > b.rank) { b.rank = rank; b.className = `btn fs-5 ${look[c][1]}`; }  // keys keep their best color
      });
      tries++;
      if (locked.every(Boolean)) { done = true; msg.textContent = "Solved! 🎉"; }
      else if (tries === maxTries) { done = true; msg.textContent = `Out of tries. The answer is ${lhs} ${answer.join("")}`; }
      else { typed = []; newRow(); msg.textContent = ""; }
      return;
    }
    full().forEach((s, i) => row.children[i + 1].textContent = s ?? "");
  }

  function reset() {
    board.replaceChildren();
    typed = []; locked = answer.map(() => false); tries = 0; done = false; msg.textContent = "";
    for (const b of Object.values(keyBtns)) { b.rank = -1; b.className = "btn btn-outline-primary fs-5"; }
    newRow();
  }

  for (const k of [...keys, "⌫", "Enter"]) {
    keyBtns[k] = html`<button style="min-width:2.5em">${k}</button>`;
    keyBtns[k].onclick = () => press(k);
    kb.append(keyBtns[k]);
  }
  resetBtn.onclick = reset;
  reset();
  return html`<div>${board}${msg}${kb}${resetBtn}</div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
// Shuffle buttons: put a carousel's slides in random order, show the new first one,
// and renumber the "1 of N" titles. Quiz questions also get renumbered in the Submit results.
// Games and answers keep any progress.
{
  for (const btn of document.querySelectorAll("[data-shuffle]")) {
    const inner = document.querySelector(btn.dataset.shuffle + " .carousel-inner");
    btn.onclick = () => d3.shuffle([...inner.children]).forEach((item, i) => {
      item.classList.toggle("active", i === 0);
      item.querySelector(".slide-num").textContent = i + 1;
      const form = item.querySelector(".quiz-question");
      if (form) form.dataset.question = `Question ${i + 1}`;
      inner.append(item);
    });
  }
}
```
